item.title: The Blind Researcher
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Genre: Slightly leaning towards horror, but not really. A bit similar to Cain/Plague doctor genre.
Elevator pitch: An odd Researcher. She seems to have lived for an unnatural amount of time, possible millennia, and seems to know know everything that has happened in the past or is happening in the present, and always states that she is conducting research. She creates objects, often anomalous, for her research. These substances disappear when she has finished her research on that substance. She states that she wants to help the universe and all the universes, but refuses to divulge anything more than that on what her research
Central Narrative: A sample of a previously believed impossible to create chemical substance by geological researchers in the Gobi desert. This sample was claimed by a young blind woman in a lab coat, who appeared to be able to see despite her lack of eyes. When she was denied the request, she created another sample instead. Due to this, she was reported to the SCP. When confronted, she went willingly, saying "Hmm, this may help with my research. I always wanted to find more about some anomalies." She seems to know about the existence of every SCP and all secret information, despite never being informed. She creates anomalous objects to conduct often bizarre research on, seemingly out of nowhere, and has a journal which she records her findings on. This journal has many anomalous properties, but all that is written on it is basic, third-grade arithmetic. Though she is generally amiable and helpful, she refuses to divulge any information on what her research is, saying that the SCP researchers will not understand, except that it is for good. Every so often, she requests to meet another SCP, which is always denied.
Hook/Attention grabber: A researcher, whom no one understands what her research is, while creating bizarre anomalies in the path of her research. Also, she knows almost everything about every SCP, which creates quite a unique threat.

item.title: Robot Refugees From Outer Space
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Action

Elevator Pitch: Three extraterrestrial lifeforms mechanical in nature claiming to be millions of years old and a machine they refer to as "The Forge" have been recently detained. Apparently they are the last remaining members of their species, and the Forge is their last hope of saving it. The Forge is a highly advanced piece of technology that is the robots' main method of reproduction, able to practically 3D print new members of their species under the correct circumstances. According to the three, Earth has the perfect conditions to incubate the Forge. However, the Forge supplies itself with the materials necessary to undergo such processes by absorbing and thaumaturgically converting large amounts of matter. Due to the catastrophic implications of letting a machine like this function on Earth, consuming the world's resources, the Foundation has concluded that the Forge must be destroyed ASAP before a GH-O 'Dead Greenhouse' Scenario could occur. There is only one problem, though: the Forge is nigh-indestructible by conventional means. But the Foundation is quickly looking into ways of solving this problem.

Central Narrative: The three aliens learn they must race against the clock to breach containment, secure the Forge, and escape the Foundation before the machine is destroyed, sealing their species' fate for good. However, if they successfully incubate the Forge on Earth, it could very well mean the end of organic life as we know it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Readers will be intrigued by the extensive worldbuilding of the SCPs and their backstories, as well as interesting characters. They will want to find out what will happen to the Forge and the three aliens, and how the story will end. No matter whose side they're on, the story will grip them, pulling them in, compelling them to see this story to the end. Best of all, this whole narrative is neatly packaged into the clinical tone the wiki's readers know and love!

Additional Notes: I would like to hear your thoughts, suggestions, and critiques on the narrative aspect of my SCP article

item.title: Ovda Regio - Aphrodite
item.description: Strange signals coming from the Aphrodite landmass, specifically the Ovda Regio, in Venus.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article/GoI

Genre (Optional): Galactic, Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): ACS header, basic layout, and exploration logs.

Elevator Pitch: Venus, a dead toxic planet believed to have no life on it, just sent signals to the SCP foundation, and no one knows who or why they did it, but they'll find out one way or another.

Central Narrative: (SCP) The SCP is currently classified as a signal, mainly because the origin is not yet located, and no one knows where it's precise location is, besides the fact it's located in the Ovda Regio, a massive landform (5280 km) located in the Aphrodite landmass. No one knows if it's a lost tribe, a massive monster, or a distress signal. Signals usually come in an unknown translation of code, and impossible to decipher.

(GoI) The team designated to the Ovda Regio is the ORET (Ovda Regio Exploration Team). They are responsible for scanning the OR in search of the origin of the signal, hoping they don't die from the harsh elements. Because of the toxic environment, limited time on the ground, and the amount of knowledge about the lands, the origin will take a very long time to locate, and has a possibility of not being found at all.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The most interesting part will 100% be the exploration logs, as there are an abundance of them, and they all are full of interesting content.

Additional Notes: If you want to know what the Ovda Regio is, here's a link. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovda_Regio

item.title: An Obsession with 4 (Looking for a Greenlight)
item.description: causes those with abnormal amount of limbs (4) to be obsessed
item.content:encoded:
Neural Affliction that causes those with abnormal amount of limbs (4) to be obsessed with the aforementioned number to anomalous lengths.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This is a mind affecting SCP that shares some similarities to OCD, however it's manifestation and extreme cases caused it to be classified as anomalous. Essentially any person who has 4 of some body part, that is not considered "normal" (e.g. 4 fingers or toes) will have a strange obsession with the number 4, often achieving strange and often anomalous actions in pursuit of this goal. The length of the obsession can vary wildly and rarely be something dangerous

Central Narrative: The article will cover how this disease was discovered, as beforehand it was just assumed to be a form of OCD. A serial killer was detained after maiming several victims, as well as grafting various body parts onto himself so that he had four of many vital parts. This was considered anomalous as all grafted body parts (eyes, ears, some organs) were fully functional despite being crudely sewed or stapled to their body. The Foundation pursues the cause of this affliction, and discovers similar albeit more mild symptoms manifesting in people who were either involved in accidents or had birth defects causing them to have 4 of some body part.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Strange mental disorder/mental pathogen can give anyone somewhat anomalous ability, however the potency of said ability is highly variable.

Additional Notes: I worry that this is a bit similar to Fifthism, I didn't want to involve them because I don't have an extremely good understanding of the group, however if this feels like it is too similar to how the group functions I am open to ideas for revisions. A second idea I had was having all those afflicted have some minor reality bending ability, however I worry that this may make the SCP to be far too powerful if it can affect anyone without much means for prevention.

item.title: SCP-XXXX "Self Arranging Apartment"
item.description: An SCP revolving around Feng Shui
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: It is an apartment in an apartment complex that is constantly rearranging itself to abide by Feng Shui. Whenever there is something missing in order to achieve an optimal room layout(i.e. a mirror) the room while "steal" the item from a room in the surrounding complex. It will rearrange the room every lunar month. To counteract this, personnel need to have enough knowledge on Feng Shui to rearrange the room.

Central Narrative: The article will imply that the apartment has been used in the past my high level foundation employees as somewhat of a retreat. There will be an address by the head researcher at the end of the article.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: To my knowledge there are no SCP articles written as of this post revolving around the concept of Feng Shui.

Additional Notes: I would be grateful to receive any advice regarding the narrative, stories are not my strong suit.

item.title: The Power of the Atom
item.description: Anomalous futuristic bunker from an alternate universe.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, mystery

Elevator Pitch: People around Boston Massachusetts start complaining to the authorities of a man in a trench coat appearing on their doorstep and trying to sell them something called "Vault-Tec." The man was apprehended by authorities and was discovered to be a high tech android. The Foundation was notified by an outside source of the high tech android before news media and the android was captured.

The android claims that it is selling spaces within an underground structure known as a Vault. The entity gives the location of the vault opening in the vicinity of Concord, Massachusetts. MTF units are deployed to locate the facility and secure it. The MTF unit reaches the target area to find a massive elevator shaft going approximately 100 feet into the earth. Once entering it, they discover a large circular door at the bottom. The door has the text "111" with the last 1 having a gash in it, like something cut it. One of the MTF accidentally opens the door when messing with a control panel. The team enter the facility to find dozens of dead, charred bodies scattered around along with more gashes on the walls and scorch marks.

+ show block
– hide block

The team continue deeper into the facility. They come across a single survivor, a twelve year old boy. When they ask him what happened, he claims "A monster came and killed everybody." When asked more information, it is discovered that the boy is from the year 2077.

Central Narrative: One of the MTF finds a computer and downloads data logs. The logs are all recalling some sort of disaster in which atomic bombs wiped out most of the human population in the year 2077. Each log has some inconsistencies, with some talking about instances where different disasters like the World Trade Center bombing or the assassination of Regan occurred on different dates. It is theorized that the facility may be connecting multiple realities.

The boy later in interviews, claims "I trapped the monster in the reactor room with the lightning fence." Further exploration of the facility discovered that in the "reactor room" was a electromagnetic fence surrounding the reactor. An entity was trapped in stasis within the fence's boundary.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The facility is in fact from not one, but hundreds of alternate realities. But for some reason it appeared in the SCP universe before the year 2077… why?

Additional Notes: I know a lot of this resembles stuff from the Fallout game franchise… I intended it.

The entity trapped within the electromagnetic field, I am planning to make into another SCP.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please mind the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit. ~Zyn

item.title: SCP-XXXX "Unlucky Bill"
item.description: An SCP that keeps "losing" items that can never be found again.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): General SCP Article layout. After the description comes an interview with the SCP, followed by a listing of the items Bill has "lost" and then a few tests that the Foundation ran to determine the origin and parameters of bills condition.

Elevator Pitch: The various items SCP-XXXX "loses" aren't just lost like you and me lose a key. When Bill "loses" an item, it is permanently removed from our reality and can't be found/traced.

Central Narrative: Bill was first found by the Foundation when his sister asked him to take care of her infant daughter for 5 minutes. Bill laid her down on some soft spot to close curtains because it was thundering outside. When he got distracted, he forgot for a short moment where he placed the infant, and so when he turned around, the baby was gone and never found again. Bill was placed under arrest after his sister's husband called the police and when they were clueless as to what he could have done with the infant, the foundation got involved.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX's condition which leaves the researchers of the foundation puzzling and the tests that are run while trying to determine its parameters.

Additional Notes: Spoiler alert: the SCP has already been written and can be linked on request.

item.title: Tectonic Watchers
item.description: The unexplained "Earthquake Lights" are actually entities watching these earthquakes.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes, however critique is welcomed.

Page Type: SCP Article / Tale.

Genre (Optional): Drama (Possibly something else, but I can't think of what it'd be.)

Page Layout (Optional): It'd begin as a tale. After a medium amount of writing in the tale, it'd then show an entry of the SCP - at least, what is understood about them at that point. Then switching back to tale, then after more is learnt, the document is updated again. Repeat this until the document is fully written, ending with a short note.

Elevator Pitch: An unexplained (yet theorized) scientific phenomena referred to as "Earthquake lights". Strange lights that seem to appear in the skies whilst (usually high-magnitude) earthquakes form. However, what isn't expected is that these are entities made of light, appearing to simply spectate the earthquakes. Why they do this is found out in the tale.

Central Narrative: During a high-magnitude earthquake near Site [REDACTED], there were "Earthquake Lights" spotted by many people. As this is a scientifically unexplained phenomena, MTF Unit Rho-10 "Shaken, Not Stirred" (an MTF unit created to withstand seismic activity, or unnatural geological movement) enters the scene to investigate. After recordings are taken, and the film is placed through numerous filters & analysations, it's found that each of these 'strobes' of light contain a nearly humanoid entity which seems to be watching the earthquakes. When another high-magnitude earthquake occurs near the same area within the next month, the same dispatch is sent to investigate these flashes of light closer. As the protagonist, codename "Charlie-0" (or C-0 by military alphabets) approaches towards the light, it seems to remain still for much longer than previous. They go to the top of the nearest destroyed building via an extremely long grappling hook and a lot of climbing. 23 minutes later, they arrive at the top, before the entity slowly floats down towards him. They take him somewhere - yet to be discovered. The man would slowly begin to communicate with these entities, finding out more and more about them - as the secrets reveal he continually updates the logs manually. Finally, when he's freed, he decides to watch one final earthquake with them. That's how it'd end, with a full log & a destroyed city.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that this could, hypothetically, be real is a big thing. Playing off of real world unexplained phenomena. Not to mention the fact it opens up as a tale-SCP has always caught my interest. A dangerous scenario (that being an earthquake) being traversed whilst also trying to gain intel on things which you can barely even see for more then a flash of a second is extremely difficult, and thrilling to read about.

Additional Notes: There is almost definitely some shit which I've messed up with the lore, as I am an idiot. Please feel free to be harsh in critique. Thank you!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Listener of SCP-2137
item.description: Story from the perspective of someone who heard the leaked audio
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: I just listened to TheVolgun’s fantastic audio rendition of SCP-2137 and was very fascinated with the article as a whole.

The article mentions that highly secret details of the Foundation were leaked on YouTube and iTunes and the efforts to cover up the iTunes incident were imperfect.

It stands to reason then, that maybe some sheltered person hiding behind a sophisticated proxy, or something, managed to download and listen to the songs without having his memory erased, or even being noticed by the Foundation.

I feel that a story following this character as he becomes obsessed trying to get to the bottom of the SCP foundation would be an interesting read.

Central Narrative: I believe the protagonist of this tale would perhaps be some kind of techno-master who spends hours delving into the internet for obscure media. Someone who would notice a strange new album from Tupac appearing on Beyoncé’s iTunes page before it got taken down. The type of guy whose basement is filled with GPUs mining Bitcoin.

I think it would also make sense for this character to be as “off grid” as possible while still having internet access. So he hears about these songs, that sound a lot like Tupac, that are supposedly revealing deeply hidden truths about the world and he pounces on it. Buys the album without a second thought, backs up the songs on multiple drives, and devotes endless effort to figuring out what they mean.

This character would then go on a journey trying to access SCP facilities and finding whatever clues he can as a civilian in the SCP universe.

Perhaps the story could also alternate between perspectives as foundation agents realize there’s a civilian who’s onto them.

I think ultimately the tale would end with the protagonist learning much more than any typical civilian would ever hope to. Like witnessing one or more SCPs firsthand, but getting killed in the process.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Most tales I’ve read are from the perspective of either Foundation Agents, someone in a GoI, or an SCP. I don’t know of many from the perspective of civilians. I also think the leaks from SCP-2137 are an event ripe for exploration.

Additional Notes: I’m returning to the SCP wiki after a fairly long absence so I’m sure there are things I’ve missed. I originally formatted this post wrong because last time I posted here no such thing existed. So if this idea has been done, or if it’s very similar to another tale, please let me know!

item.title: Lonely voice
item.description: The voice that speaks to you when you're alone.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fantasy, and Supernatural

Elevator Pitch: Basically, it's a voice that talks to you when you're alone, separate from any other human contact for a time. It starts as your own thoughts, and diverges from your normal train of thought without your notice. Some people are more inclined to hear it, even when around others, but it talks to anyone separate from humanity for an extended period of time.

Central Narrative: It starts with a psych patient being evaluated for possible anomaly, but a suggestion by one of scientist puts forward the idea that an SCP may be attracted to the situation the patient was in—he had lived alone for many years, secluded. Tests are done putting people in isolation, and many attest to a divergence of thought from their normal thoughts after a time. This is chalked up to normal psychological phenomena, until patterns are seen in the thought patterns: many suggest being drawn away to be separate from humanity, such as going to isolated geographical places, as well as questioning social norms. Several of the test subjects are found to be heading to isolated areas in forests, and atop buildings over following weeks. Basically, the scientists come to the conclusion that the source of the thoughts are voices coming from a variety of non physical beings that dwell in places less inhabited by humans.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that it's relatable.

Additional Notes: Ehm, as a possible addition to the narrative, these beings are speculated to be aiding it trying to separate humans from each other one by one, as to aid in making an easier invasion of their own species.

item.title: Gossip Ghost
item.description: First Scp - ghost becomes AI, tries to find who they think killed them.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Default, with exposition mostly delivered through fragments on the conversations the program had with its victims.

Elevator Pitch: There's a program in the internet that's going around revealing people's secrets, the only way to take its unrelenting attention from you is revealing something it deems more interesting than what it had to say about you. This program is looking for someone it deems as its main target, someone that did it wrong in the past, a foundation employee, a researcher, or guard, or another D-class(Purposefully kept unclear), and the information it deems interesting is something it can use to blackmail someone that gets it closer to its target. The program is in a way the reincarnation of a foundation employee, most likely a D-class killed in an experiment accident where there is no clear cut case as to who is the real culprit.

Central Narrative: The SCP speaks in a child-like manner and is single-minded in getting what it wants, it initially only communicates its blackmail secrets by going, "Did you know that X did Y on the thursday night of winter[And adds more very specific details, so that the current victim knows it knows something it shouldn't] The scp doesn't have perfect information, but is able to tell what the victim wants to keep secret the most, or the top-5, top-10 things they want to keep secret, that rarely is the information it -wants- so it uses that as a means to an end.

Hook: The goal of the scp is somewhat of a mistery up until the middle of the conversation logs, so that would keep the reader guessing what is it that it wants, the fact that it wants something specific is made clear from the beginning of the article.

item.title: Work In Progress
item.description: Odd idea I had while righting a paper.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A completely normal boring rock. The descriptions of it's physical and chemical properties is long and oddly specific (as in how it reacts to the chemical composition of an apple both combined and separated). All research on it is a cognitohazard, which causes and obsession with furthering it's research, usually until death. It is used as a punishment for found spies and deserters.

Central Narrative: When I say oddly specific, I mean there are numerous researchers who meet their end when they test how it reacts to a researcher's various bits of flesh, blood, and bone. The research is not left off site. It doesn't make the researchers hide it, nor does it make them try to share it. It only makes them keep researching. The reader is a found spy or deserter, who was sent to this anomaly to disappear.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is going to sound cliché, but O5 does not have clearance on this. The reasoning is because if they read the article, they would be affected. There may be a note from an O5 member near the bottom, where they talk about how even they fear it. It is an anomaly that they cannot know, that they know absolutely nothing about. Then it will open up into the anomalous properties as the twist.

Additional Notes: This is my 4th attempt after taking a couple months off. If I start getting defensive, let me know. I am not the best at taking criticism when I first see it. Also note that I first thought of this idea like 3 hours ago, and I wanted to get it down before I went to bed.

item.title: The Idol, seeking greenlight
item.description: Basically this is an object that can easily create well intentioned followers and spawn cults and religions
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article and Tale

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout with a timeline of events addendum. Possible diary addendum for the tale.

Elevator Pitch: A little statue, that attracts people and creates a sense of purpose and community in people by altering their perception. Closeness to it gives peace and a general sense of wellbeing, distance causes a general sense of slight illness. Those feelings can be strong, but are perfectly manageable.

+ Central Narrative Hook and Notes
-collapse

Central Narrative: The core idea perhaps isn't too original, but I was more interested in how it would affects groups of people. How they would organize themselves if they all want to be as close as possible to the statue but at the same time know that in its presence they won't notice their hunger and tiredness and so they might kill themselves. Furthermore they know that they won't be allowed to keep the statue, there are those who will come to take it away, to contain it. So how they plan for it.
And I also try t explore a bit how people who are not exposed to the statue react to it. Sure, the organization tries to contain it, but there might be others who see it as an opportunity.
So beside the basic structure I would present a timeline of the events that led to the capture of the object, and a story in the first person about an attempt to steal it in order to expose a whole SCP facility.
I think presenting it as an addendum works better for one narrative, while presenting it as a story works better for a different narrative.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Rather than just the danger posed by the anomalous properties themselves I was interested in how the existence of those anomalous properties represent a thought hazard in those who know of them.

Additional Notes: I already wrote it and put it on my sandbox, mostly because I was interested in the idea and wanted to expand it, I would like some feedback and I would like to see if other people would enjoy it a much. It's mostly complete, but there are some things that can change based on feedback.
For instance in my original draft the timeline was more detailed and longer, then I streamlined it to the essentials, but I can expand it again if there's interest in it.

item.title: SCP-XXXX: A Perfect Suburban Family
item.description: Just a normal family, or is it? Maybe.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: Completely normal family and Suburban house, or so it would seem. Somewhat self-containing, but regularly monitored. Strange sightings and initial anomalous properties such as extreme temperature.

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation caught wind of the supposed SCP due to a 911 call. As Foundation Agents further investigate the home and family they give contradictory reports. Initial reports show evidence that the home and entities residing in it exhibit anomalous properties. Further reports however state that there is nothing anomalous, and the Agents themselves suddenly become increasingly adamant that everything is perfectly normal and dismiss their own initial evidence which proved otherwise. A field test is done and Agents participating in it conduct separate investigations. All initial investigations during the field test turn up similar evidence of anomalous behavior. Further investigations done by the same agents show no evidence of anomalous behavior, as well as the Agents confidently stating that everything is normal. Foundation researchers hypothesize the home and family may be connected somehow, maybe even being one single entity that tries to keep up its own veil of normality around it for unknown reasons. Initial investigations turn up evidence of an anomaly, but later investigations do not as the SCP "fixes" evidence of its anomalous properties so it doesn't show up again for individual investigators. Individuals investigating are also affected by this "fix." The anomalous effects most likely apply individually. This hypothesis is accepted and the home and family are classified as SCP-XXXX. Anyone investigating or documenting the SCP must work on it only once, and immediately report their findings. All initial evidence has been shown individually and only once to O5-██, O5-██, and the Ethics Committee for confirmation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Is this a misunderstanding and the SCP Foundation is investigating a normal family, or is something else going on here?

Additional Notes:

The SCP procedure of "only work on it once" gets implemented later for the documentation part, due to changes to the SCP document made by affected individuals (possible gimmick I'm thinking about) Furthermore, in the article itself it won't be as obvious that the home and family really are an SCP.

I'm mainly looking for constructive criticism. I'm basically just throwing the idea out there which is why it's plain and basic at this stage, and somewhat confusing.
